investigation.found: Priya Shah's August timesheet for Acme Corp came in with 156 hours, but nothing in it shows that anyone at Acme signed off on those hours — there is no approver name and no approval date. Because the agent only invoices hours the client has approved, it held the item instead of billing it. There is nothing else wrong: this is the only item for Priya, no invoice has been started, and the agent's invoice records are clean, so the single missing fact is who approved and when.
evidence: Item 1: Priya Shah, Acme Corp, Aug 1–31 2026, status needs_review, 156.00 hours, approval: none shown
One open review on the item: NO_APPROVAL — no client approval visible
Item history shows only creation and the status change — no approval was ever recorded
This is the only timesheet item on file, so there is no second or corrected copy of this timesheet
No invoices recorded for this item and no invoice problems anywhere in QuickBooks

proposals.what_to_do: If you know who at Acme approved Priya's August hours, tell the agent the name and the date and it will invoice the 156 hours.
proposals.why: Right when the approval exists (a reply, a portal sign-off, a verbal OK) and only needs recording — replace the name and date with the real ones.

proposals.what_to_do: Ask Priya or the Acme manager to send the approved timesheet, and when the approved copy arrives tell the agent to use it instead of the one it has.
